title: [SEC-CON-001] Freeze the current secret-management contract inventory

<!-- falcone-secrets:SEC-CON-001 -->

Parent: [SEC-CON](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/1)

## User story

As a Falcone maintainer, I want versioned fixtures for every secret consumer, so that migration preserves existing behavior.

## Description

Versioned fixtures for every secret consumer.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-CON-001-1**: The project must inventory every OpenBao client, mount, auth path, secret reference, rotation consumer and non-OpenBao key lifecycle against a pinned Falcone commit.
- **FR-CON-001-2**: The system must preserve approved Falcone API routes, metadata fields, status codes and error precedence through contract tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cover workspace secret CRUD, inventory domains, rotation, consumer acknowledgements, BYOK, function projection and workflow credential references.
- [ ] Distinguish code, documentation, deployment evidence and planned sibling-service contracts; record actual OpenBao/ESO versions separately.
- [ ] Identify direct Vault-compatible callers and make an explicit adapter/retirement decision for each; do not promise the entire Vault API.

## Dependencies

None; discovery can begin independently.

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [SEC-CON-002] Define ownership and first-party service boundaries

Parent: [SEC-CON](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/1)

## User story

As a platform architect, I want one owner per secret, policy, credential and projection, so that services do not compete to manage security state.

## Description

One owner per secret, policy, credential and projection.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-CON-002-1**: The system must define a single authoritative writer for secret versions, rotation state, leases, policies and backend credentials throughout migration.
- **FR-CON-002-2**: Falcone IAM must remain the owner of users, roles and federation, while Falcone quota services remain the owner of entitlements and accounting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document IAM/secrets/bootstrap dependencies and the transition from OpenBao to falcone-secrets without modifying sibling repositories implicitly.
- [ ] Map legacy domains platform, tenant, functions, gateway and iam to canonical scoped resources; ownership is not inferred from a caller path.
- [ ] Separate operator bootstrap material, IAM session credentials, backend credentials and tenant application secrets, with named custodians.

title: [SEC-AUTH-001] Integrate user and service authorization with Falcone IAM

<!-- falcone-secrets:SEC-AUTH-001 -->

Parent: [SEC-AUTH](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/2)

## User story

As a service owner, I want audience-bound identities and scoped authorization decisions, so that secrets are accessible only to approved callers.

## Description

Audience-bound identities and scoped authorization decisions.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-AUTH-001-1**: Every online secret operation must authenticate its caller and authorize action, resource, tenant/workspace, audience and delegated authority.
- **FR-AUTH-001-2**: Metadata listing, value resolution, key use, key administration, rotation and destruction must be distinct permissions with deny-by-default behavior.

- [ ] Test Keycloak-era and falcone-iam adapters without adding a second login/federation stack to secrets; preserve SAML/OIDC/LDAP/AD/SCIM identity handling through IAM.
- [ ] Reject forged gateway headers, wrong audiences, cross-tenant IDs, untrusted resource owners and stale policy revisions.
- [ ] Preserve current public role/error contracts through an adapter while reviewing legacy role-name aliases; a platform role does not automatically reveal values.

title: [SEC-KV-001] Implement write-only workspace secret CRUD

<!-- falcone-secrets:SEC-KV-001 -->

Parent: [SEC-KV](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/3)

As a workspace administrator, I want the existing Falcone secret APIs on the new backend, so that applications can migrate without exposing their values.

- [ ] Preserve secretName/name alias, timestamps, description and resolvedRefCount; expose neither value nor internal version through FunctionWorkspaceSecret.
- [ ] Enforce the current name rule and value limit, sanitized failures and reference-registry errors; no console reveal action is introduced.

title: [SEC-KV-002] Implement internal versions, concurrency and retention
body:
<!-- falcone-secrets:SEC-KV-002 -->

Parent: [SEC-KV](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/3)

## User story

As a service developer, I want immutable internal versions and compare-and-swap writes, so that concurrent updates cannot silently corrupt state.

## Description

Immutable internal versions and compare-and-swap writes.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-KV-002-1**: The store must assign immutable version IDs and use atomic revision checks for create/replace, active-version selection and metadata changes.
- **FR-KV-002-2**: Internal soft deletion, recovery and irreversible destruction must be distinct operations with explicit retention and authorization rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test concurrent writers, idempotency-key conflicts, retry after commit and references pinned to removed versions.
- [ ] Do not turn the existing public delete-all route into a recoverable soft delete or resurrect a revoked version through rollback.
- [ ] Document backup retention and historical-key exposure: deleting live records is not proof of immediate physical erasure from every backup.

## Dependencies

[SEC-KV-001](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/21)

title: [SEC-KEY-001] Implement authenticated envelope encryption
body:
<!-- falcone-secrets:SEC-KEY-001 -->

Parent: [SEC-KEY](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/4)

## User story

As a security engineer, I want encrypted values bound to their resource context, so that database access alone cannot reveal or relocate secrets.

## Description

Encrypted values bound to their resource context.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-KEY-001-1**: Secret values must use reviewed authenticated encryption with fresh per-version data keys and authenticated tenant/resource/version context.
- **FR-KEY-001-2**: Root key-encryption authority must be outside the ciphertext database, with a documented KMS/HSM or approved operator-unlock custody profile.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use a supported AEAD library and managed nonce generation; reject modified ciphertext, AAD, key IDs and cross-resource substitution.
- [ ] Store only ciphertext, wrapped data keys and required metadata; PostgreSQL/WAL and backups must never contain plaintext value columns.
- [ ] Separate platform/domain wrapping keys where policy requires; document that an online authorized service can still decrypt and process values.

## Dependencies

[SEC-CON-003](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/17), [SEC-BOOT-001](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/27)

title: [SEC-KEY-002] Implement key rotation, rewrap and compromise response
body:
<!-- falcone-secrets:SEC-KEY-002 -->

Parent: [SEC-KEY](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/4)

## User story

As a key custodian, I want versioned key rotation and resumable rewrapping, so that key replacement does not lose data or revive compromised access.

## Description

Versioned key rotation and resumable rewrapping.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-KEY-002-1**: Key rotation must distinguish root/KEK rewrapping, data-key re-encryption and external credential replacement, with separate state and permissions.
- **FR-KEY-002-2**: Old keys must not be destroyed until retained ciphertext, backups and restore requirements have been reconciled under an approved retirement policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resume interrupted batches with checkpoints and compare-and-swap; concurrent writes use the designated active key version.
- [ ] Test mixed replicas, KMS outage and lost acknowledgements without claiming rewrap re-encrypts plaintext under a fresh data key.
- [ ] Emergency key compromise procedures include external credential rotation and assessed backup exposure; rewrapping alone cannot undo prior key compromise.

## Dependencies

[SEC-KEY-001](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/24)

title: [SEC-KEY-003] Protect memory, transport and key-provider boundaries

Parent: [SEC-KEY](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-secrets/issues/4)

## User story

As a security operator, I want explicit plaintext exposure and transport limits, so that the implementation avoids misleading encryption guarantees.

## Description

Explicit plaintext exposure and transport limits.

Phase: P2 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-KEY-003-1**: All value-bearing service traffic must use authenticated TLS and explicit size/time limits, with debugging and request-body capture disabled in production.
- **FR-KEY-003-2**: Key-provider interfaces must distinguish non-exportable operations from exported software keys and fail safely on unsupported algorithms or custody mode.

- [ ] Exclude values from logs, traces, core dumps, metrics and error bodies; qualify crash diagnostics and proxy capture settings.
- [ ] Document Node/GC zeroization limits, ephemeral plaintext lifetime and optional isolated crypto workers; never claim guaranteed process-memory erasure.
- [ ] Exercise provider outages, invalid certificates, algorithm mismatch and excessive decrypt/sign requests with bounded resource use.

- **FR-DEV-003-1**: A release candidate must pass cross-tenant, tamper, replay, stale-policy, secret-leakage and dependency-failure tests for all enabled engines and delivery paths.
- **FR-DEV-003-2**: Production cutover must require independent security review of key custody, bootstrap, secret handling, authorization and external revocation guarantees.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test modified AAD/ciphertext, wrong-key signing, forged consumer ACK, path injection, untrusted guest input and SSRF during provider use.
- [ ] Inject crashes around audit/DB commit, provider activation, outbox delivery and key rotation; verify declared failure and recovery behavior.
- [ ] Record residual memory/cluster-admin exposure, evidence gaps and owned exceptions; container hardening is not hostile-code isolation or a compliance certificate.
